title: Changelog conflict resolver at landing
lead: When the base branch moved and the merge of it into the slice branch conflicts only in the root `CHANGELOG.md`, ork resolves that file itself with `git merge-file --union` (branch side first), commits the merge and goes on with the landing. Any other conflict goes to the one implementer fix round, as today.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Parity row 5.4 and gap 15 (`docs/orchestrator-parity.md:90`, `:142`). When the base branch moved, landing merges it into the slice branch in the worktree (`internal/engine/land.go:136`). A conflict stays in place and goes to one implementer fix round; a second block stops the run (`internal/engine/land.go:137-146`, `internal/engine/land.go:177-193`, `docs/design.md:425-432`). Changelog conflicts are listed as after v1 (`docs/manual-steps.md:7-8`, and the row at `:62`). ork's `CHANGELOG.md` has one `## Unreleased` list with one entry per slice at the top, so two slices that land in turn conflict on every merge. A role fix round for a pure append conflict is slow and costs tokens. Slicer has no changelog resolver (`slicer find changelog` and `slicer find "merge driver"` list only the render merge driver for generated files). Git has the union merge: `git merge-file --union` and the `merge=union` attribute.

Owner decisions, 2026-10-29 (interactive; the S180 note), recorded and not changed here:

1. Mechanism: an ork step in `mergeBaseIn` that runs `git merge-file --union`. (Not a `.gitattributes` line, since ork writes nothing inside a project, `docs/state.md:23-26`; not a role.)
2. Files: only the root `CHANGELOG.md` (no registry field).
3. Entry order: the branch side first.
4. No note to the owner: the resolution is silent. So this is not a UI slice.

Owner, 2026-10-29: v1.1, not v1.0. Design (*proposed* until an adj record decides it): the steps below. Every git call is a logged write (`writes[]`, `internal/runrec/writer.go:66`).

Wave class: this slice touches `internal/engine`, so it is the one engine-class slice of its wave.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `internal/engine/land.go:135-146` (the conflict branch of `mergeBaseIn`; `mergeBaseIn` is `:110-175`, `landBlocked` is `:179-193`).
- `internal/engine/changelog.go` (new: `resolveChangelog`).
- `internal/engine/changelog_test.go` (new).
- `internal/engine/land_test.go:45-53` (the fake git script gains one-shot failure switches for `merge-file`, `add` and `commit`) and tests beside `TestLandConflictRunsOneFixRoundThenReturnsToApproval` at `:557`.
- `docs/design.md:400-409` (landing step 1) and `docs/design.md:425-432` (the conflict paragraph).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
All in `internal/engine`, with real git in temp repos through `newLandEnv` (`land_test.go:101`). To make a changelog conflict: commit a `CHANGELOG.md` to the base with `env.moveBase` and merge `main` into the worktree branch, write the branch's entry at the top in the worktree, then `env.moveBase` another entry at the same place.

- `TestLandResolvesAChangelogOnlyConflict`: both entries stay, the branch's first, with no conflict markers; the landing reaches the fast-forward and `slicer land`; `land_fixes` is 0; no implementer round runs. Fails first: today the run goes to the fix round (`LandFixes` is 1).
- `TestLandChangelogResolutionCommitsTheMerge`: the commit message is `Merge BASE into BRANCH` (for example `Merge main into S04`), the merge has two parents, and the calls (`merge-file`, `add`, `commit`) are in `writes[]`. Fails first: no such calls.
- `TestLandLeavesOtherConflictsToTheFixRound`: a conflict in `CHANGELOG.md` and in `shared.txt` changes nothing: no `merge-file` call, both files still unmerged at the start of the fix round, one fix round as today. `TestLandConflictRunsOneFixRoundThenReturnsToApproval` (`land_test.go:557`) and `TestLandConflictTwiceStopsAndKeepsTheWorktree` (`:665`) stay green.
- `TestLandChangelogResolverIgnoresOtherChangelogNames`: a conflict in `docs/CHANGELOG.md` alone is not resolved (no `merge-file` call; fix round as today).
- `TestLandChangelogResolverFailureFallsBack`: with `merge-file` failing, and again with `add` failing, the conflict is still in the worktree (the file has conflict markers and is unmerged) and the run goes to the fix round with `LandFixes` 1. After the `add` failure ork restores the markers (`git checkout --merge -- CHANGELOG.md`); it never runs `--abort` or `reset`.
- `TestLandChangelogMergeCommitFailureGoesToTheFixRound`: with the final `commit` failing after a good `add`, the run goes to the fix round and the brief names the failed commit.
- `TestLandChangelogResolverNeedsAllThreeStages`: a changelog that both sides added (no common ancestor stage) is left to the fix round.

sections.heading: Implement
Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- `go test -race -count=1 ./internal/engine -run 'TestLand'`.
- `rg -n "abort|reset" internal/engine/changelog.go` prints nothing.
- [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] The owner restarts the daemon when no role runs (`ork daemon restart` refuses while one runs unless `--force`, `docs/guide.md:391`), then lands two slices in turn that both add a `CHANGELOG.md` entry, and sees the second land with no fix round and both entries in the file.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Landing: merge changelog-only conflicts with git merge-file --union".
